papers.key_finding: MP-associated biofilms increase cell density, retain extracellular DNA, and promote intercellular contact, facilitating plasmid conjugation and, in some experimental systems, transformation; field evidence demonstrates particle occurrence and ecological ARG enrichment, whereas direct transfer is best shown in defined experimental systems.
papers.title: Recent advances in understanding the impact of microplastics on bacterial antibiotic resistance: mechanisms, evidence gaps, and One Health implications
papers.tldr: A review conceptualizing microplastics as mobile evolutionary interfaces where biofilms accumulate antibiotic resistance genes and can promote horizontal gene transfer, while noting that enrichment alone does not establish clinical risk.
papers.why_relevant: Directly relevant to Fangzhou's interests in antibiotic resistance and microbial population and community ecology, since it frames how surface-associated biofilm growth and horizontal gene transfer shape the spread of resistance determinants across environmental microbial communities.

papers.key_finding: Optimal phage diversity emerges from a trade-off between niche differentiation, which increases with host phenotypic heterogeneity, and reduced host abundance in each phage's preferred niche, with the optimum set by the match between host phenotypic dispersion and phage niche width.
papers.title: Intermediate phenotypic heterogeneity creates an optimal coexistence window in bacteria–phage communities
papers.tldr: A trait-based modeling study finds that phage richness in bacteria-phage communities is maximized at an intermediate level of host growth-rate heterogeneity rather than increasing monotonically.
papers.why_relevant: Connects to Fangzhou's work on microbial population dynamics and community ecology and to growth-rate heterogeneity in bacterial physiology, providing a quantitative principle for how intraspecific phenotypic variation shapes coexistence and biodiversity.

papers.key_finding: In an example simulation of an underground hydrogen storage with active methanogens, substrates (H2 and CO2) do not become limiting in large parts of the storage, so microbial populations grow to maximum density and continuously convert hydrogen and carbon dioxide into methane, strongly coupling with flow and transport.
papers.title: Model development for microbial growth in underground hydrogen storage reservoirs
papers.tldr: A new bio-reactive transport model for underground hydrogen storage couples substrate-limited Monod microbial growth with an added maximum-density limitation and flow and transport in a two-phase porous medium.
papers.why_relevant: Relevant to Fangzhou's interests in microbial growth laws, dynamic metabolism, and population dynamics, as it extends substrate-limited growth models with a density cap and couples them to environmental transport in a subsurface community context.

papers.key_finding: Dioszegia facilitates Albugo colonization by alleviating its thiamine auxotrophy through cross-feeding, and genomic and transcriptomic analyses indicate natural selection has acted on thiamine production in Dioszegia, shaping this metabolic complementation.
papers.title: Thiamine cross-feeding drives microbial coexistence in the leaf microbiome
papers.tldr: A continental-scale leaf microbiome survey identifies an asymmetric mutualism in which the yeast Dioszegia hungarica supplies thiamine via a dedicated membrane permease to the auxotrophic oomycete Albugo laibachii, promoting their coexistence.
papers.why_relevant: Directly relevant to Fangzhou's interests in microbial community ecology, metabolic cross-feeding, and nutrient-driven coexistence, showing how a specific biosynthetic pathway and transporter mediate community assembly and stability in a plant microbiome.

papers.key_finding: Nutrient availability in the medium and microbial stress responses were key determinants of in vitro community establishment, and mucin glycan metabolism in RapidAIM medium supported Bacteroidaceae species poorly supported in other media, yielding a community most similar to the uncultured fecal inoculum.
papers.title: Dissecting functional dynamics of fecal-derived in vitro stable microbial communities with metaproteomics
papers.tldr: Large-scale quantitative metaproteomics tracked functional and community dynamics of human fecal microbiomes cultured in three media over 25 serial passages, showing that both medium and donor characteristics shape community establishment.
papers.why_relevant: Relevant to Fangzhou's interests in microbial population dynamics and community ecology, as it uses metaproteomics to link specific nutrient substrates and stress responses to which taxa persist in an in vitro gut community.

papers.key_finding: A microbial succession involving chemoheterotrophic and nitrogen-fixing bacteria predicts functions in biomineralization of nitrogen- and phosphorus-containing compounds, and this rapid decomposition triggers swift phosphorus release that can fuel coastal eutrophication.
papers.title: Microbial community dynamics mediate rapid biomass loss and phosphorus recycling in pelagic Sargassum
papers.tldr: A study of pelagic Sargassum characterizes rapid biomass decomposition with a 16-day litter half-life and nutrient release, alongside a bacterial microbiome succession during decay.
papers.why_relevant: Relevant to Fangzhou's interests in microbial community ecology and nutrient cycling, as it links stage-specific bacterial community succession to the mineralization of algal litter and the release of phosphorus in a marine system.

papers.key_finding: PdC inoculation consistently improved fermentation kinetics compared with spontaneous fermentation, particularly at 13% potential alcohol, and preserved higher Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain diversity than commercial inoculation while an indigenous strain showed strong competitive ability against QA23.
papers.title: Grape ripeness shapes microbial community dynamics and fermentation outcomes during modified pied de cuve wine fermentations
papers.tldr: A wine fermentation study shows that grape ripeness shapes bacterial and fungal community composition and fermentation outcomes when using a modified pied de cuve inoculation strategy compared with commercial inoculation and spontaneous fermentation.
papers.why_relevant: Directly relevant to Fangzhou's interests in fermentation ecology, microbial population dynamics, and community ecology, as it examines how an ecological driver (grape ripeness) and inoculation strategy shape strain diversity and community succession during alcoholic fermentation.

papers.key_finding: For an antithetic integral feedback controller on a two-species gene-expression cascade, a tensor-product Bernstein enclosure certifies 83.2% of the design plane versus 50.9-58.9% for baseline enclosures, and for a fifth-order loop the certified fraction increases from 34.4% to 73.8%.
papers.title: Certified Design Regions under Parametric Plant Uncertainty with Application to Antithetic Integral Feedback
papers.tldr: A preprint formulates robust controller tuning under parametric plant uncertainty as a set-inversion problem and computes certified design regions for antithetic integral feedback controllers using validated range enclosures.
papers.why_relevant: Relevant to Fangzhou's interests in biomolecular reaction networks, cell-fate circuits, and data-driven design of biological networks, as it provides certified design regions for controllers acting on gene-expression cascades under parameter uncertainty, though it is an enabling computational method rather than a biological study.
